name: Dominica
summary: A mountainous, forested island, independent in 1978; home to the last Kalinago (Island Carib) territory.

knownFor.label: Kalinago Territory
knownFor.note: Land of the Indigenous Kalinago people.

location.value: Windward Islands of the Lesser Antilles; 750 km².

climate.value: Tropical, with a hurricane season from June to November.

resources.value: Bananas, volcanic mineral springs, and tourism based on the rainforest and nature trails.

disasters.value: Hurricane Maria (2017) devastated the island, destroying much housing and farming.

population.value: About 72,000 (2021 estimate); 71,293 at the 2011 census (the article’s figures vary).

urbanisation.value: Most people live in and around the capital.

disease.value: Dengue occurs, and basic health care is good for a small island.

migration.value: Emigration (to other countries) is the main reason population growth is slow.

economicBase.value: Farming and eco-tourism; citizenship by investment, valued at 16% of government revenue (2018).

tradeRoutes.value: The port of Roseau handles cruise ships and cargo.

wealth.value: Not stated as an income group in the article read; HDI 0.761, rated “high” (98th, 2023).

moneyAndTax.value: The Eastern Caribbean dollar, shared with several neighbouring islands.

inequality.value: Large gaps between the capital and rural areas.

governmentType.value: A parliamentary republic in the Commonwealth.

keyRulers.value: Eugenia Charles, called the Caribbean’s first female prime minister, after the 1980 election.

succession.value: Elections to the House of Assembly choose the prime minister.

stability.value: A stable democracy since independence, apart from a coup attempt in 1981.

eliteConflict.value: Competition between political parties and leaders.

armyAndTech.value: Police and a small defence or coast-guard force.

majorWars.value: France and Britain fought over the island until Britain took it in 1763.

alliancesRivals.value: A member of the Commonwealth, CARICOM and the Organisation of Eastern Caribbean States.

inventions.value: No major inventions are associated with the modern state.

scienceEducation.value: Schools; University of the West Indies campuses nearby.

openness.value: Open to trade and foreign investment, with periods of restriction.

communicationTransport.value: Roads, small airports and ferries to the neighbouring French islands.

religion.value: Mostly Christian (Catholic), with Rastafarian and Kalinago traditions.

languageWriting.value: English; Dominican Creole French (Komwèl Donmnik), widely spoken but used less by younger generations.

artsArchitecture.value: Creole festivals and the World Creole Music Festival (the article does not mention Carnival or soca).

socialStructure.value: Mostly of African descent; Kalinago minority.

sharedIdentity.value: An island and Caribbean identity, with pride in the Kalinago people and the “Nature Isle” image.

dailyLife.value: Houses; fish, breadfruit, rice and peas.

neighbours.value: The French islands of Guadeloupe (north) and Martinique (south).

ideasReligions.value: Brown Privilege Bill (1831) and Slavery Abolition Act (1833); Dominica was the first British West Indies colony with an African-majority elected legislature (1838).

colonisation.value: British from 1763 by the Treaty of Paris; France recaptured it 1778–1783; associated state 1967; independent 3 November 1978.

riseSignals.value: Independent republic on 3 November 1978, under Prime Minister Patrick John.

declineSignals.value: None that define the country as a whole.

outcome.value: Dominica continues as an independent republic.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts are well documented; some figures are estimates.
